title: Lightning Onboard: 24-72h Activation Kit
body:
Purpose and scope:
This one-pager is a condensed, low-friction onboarding sprint designed for hires who need to be productive in the first 24–72 hours. It’s intended for ICs, contractors, and lateral transfers who already have basic tooling experience. Use as a supplement to the full onboarding playbook when speed and minimal context switching are prioritized.

How to use this doc:
- Hiring manager or onboarding lead shares link before start-of-day 1.
- Buddy completes their prep checklist 24h before the new hire joins.
- HR confirms account provisioning windows and escalation path.
- Treat as a living sprint—mark items done inline and log blockers under "Immediate blockers."

Outcome in 72 hours:
- New hire has working dev environment or product-facing account, first small deliverable underway, and a clear 30-day priority list.
- Manager, buddy, and the hire have aligned expectations and a short list of measurable signals for success (see "Conversion & success signals").

Day 0 (pre-start) - Manager & Buddy prep (24h before)
- Manager: send welcome note with start agenda, org chart snippet, and first-week objectives (3 bullets).
- Buddy: validate access matrix with infra (VPN, GitHub org invite, SSO groups). Confirm CI tokens or API keys if required.
- People Ops: confirm payroll/contract paperwork done, health & benefits primers sent.
- Optional: short "welcome pack" with team glossary, key Slack channels, and a 5-min recording introducing the team.

Day 1 (0–8 hours) - Kickoff & friction removal
Manager tasks:
- 30-min check-in: role expectations, 30/60/90 outline (high level), immediate priorities.
- Share a single actionable task that results in a public artifact (e.g., small docs change, tiny bug fix, simple infra runbook).

Buddy tasks:
- 1:1 intro (30–60min): walk through day-to-day, show dev flow/PR process, highlight common pitfalls.
- Walkthrough of working environment: clone, build, run tests (or show console and one smoke run for product roles).
- Quick list of 5 standard commands or dashboards the hire will use day-to-day.

People Ops tasks:
- Confirm access to payroll, calendar, and benefits portals.
- Share code of conduct and workplace safety/remote-work expectations.

Deliverable by end of day 1:
- A tiny public artifact: a documented README update, a reproducible smoke test, or a customer-facing micro-edit.
- New hire posts a short "day-1 note" in the designated Slack channel summarizing what they did and any blockers.

Day 2 (24–48 hours) - Short feedback loop and context building
Manager tasks:
- 20-min sync: review deliverable, give concrete feedback, confirm next micro-project (2–4 hour scope).
- Add the hire to a primary ongoing project board with one prioritized card assigned.

Buddy tasks:
- Pair session (1–2 hours) focused on the primary project. Share architecture/topology map and common tickets.
- Highlight 3 stakeholders the hire should know (names, roles, how they interact).

People Ops tasks:
- Check-in: confirm benefits enrollment timeline and remind about any optional orientation events.

Deliverable by end of day 2:
- Progress on the assigned card; at least one PR or a detailed research note with next steps.

Day 3 (48–72 hours) - Solidify momentum and success criteria
Manager tasks:
- 30-min review: evaluate deliverables, align on 30-day goals with measurable checkpoints.
- Schedule weekly 1:1 cadence and a 30-day review checkpoint.

Buddy tasks:
- Knowledge transfer handoff: a short checklist of recurring operational tasks the hire will own.
- Introduce the hire to one cross-functional partner in a short intro call.

People Ops tasks:
- Invite to optional new-joiner retrospective (end of week) and collect pulse.

Deliverable by end of day 3:
- A working branch/feature or a cross-team note with actionable next steps; manager confirms at least two success signals for the 30-day review.

Conversion & success signals (early indicators)
- Technical: new hire submitted a PR that passes CI or provided a deployable doc/process update.
- Product/Customer: created a ticket or note that meaningfully reduces a known customer friction point.
- Engagement: attended two team rituals and posted in the team channel with a substantive update.
- Autonomy: can reproduce a core workflow end-to-end with <2 interruptions.

Mentorship & inclusion micro-practices
- Start every pair session with a 5-min "context checkpoint" so the hire can ask clarifying Qs.
- Avoid relying on tribal knowledge—record short Looms for recurring ops.
- Buddy should proactively surface resources for major accessibility considerations (e.g., captions, font sizes).
- Invite the hire to a rotating "introduction slot" on a team sync to incubate confidence.

Checklist: immediate access items (yes/no)
- SSO/G Suite access
- Slack and primary team channels
- GitHub/org access with necessary repo perms
- VPN or corp network access
- CI/CD dashboard access or read-only links
- Key internal dashboards (billing/observability/product metrics)
- HR/Payroll login
- Equipment shipped and verified (if remote)

Common blockers & escalation path
- Access delays > 24h: escalate to IT Ops with ticket template (include hire name, start date, needed groups).
- Payroll/contract discrepancies: escalate to People Ops lead (people-ops@redwood.com) and cc hiring manager.
- Critical tooling failure: open SRE/Infra pager if the issue blocks basic operations.

Lightweight interview rubric for quick hiring decisions (for contractors/fast fills)
- Core skill probe (40%): 20–30 minute live task focused on actual work product. Does candidate produce a small, verifiable artifact?
- Communication & collaboration (25%): clarity, responsiveness, how they document assumptions.
- Cultural fit (15%): alignment with team norms (feedback receptivity, cross-team empathy).
- Risk & ramp (20%): estimated time to independent contribution; flag special onboarding needs.

Templates and micro-forms (copy & paste)
- Day-1 welcome note (manager):
  "Hi [Name], welcome! Today's outline: 10am intro w/manager; 11am buddy setup & env walkthrough; 2pm first micro-task. Slack: @[buddy] for questions. See you soon. —[Manager]"

- Quick blocker escalation (to IT Ops):
  "New hire [Name], start [Date], missing access: GitHub org invite + VPN group. Ticket created at [time]. Contact: [manager email]."

Notes and follow-ups
- Keep this document minimal; link to the canonical onboarding binder for longer policies and benefits details.
- Capture retrospective notes at the end of week 1 and feed into the people-ops "onboarding signal" dashboard.

Appendix: low-effort signals to track (for people ops)
- % of hires completing day-1 artifact (target 95%)
- % with all required access within 24h (target 98%)
- Self-reported confidence score (end of day 3) on a 1–5 scale (target >=4)

Immediate blockers (if any):
- [space for manager to paste live notes]"
